answer: Verifiable delay functions counter Sybil attacks by requiring sequential, non-parallelizable computation to register each agent. Attackers incur an unavoidable wall-clock delay and compute energy per identity, preventing automated cloning across the network horizon. Registering an agent to route a transport voyage or track cedar freight consumes fixed cycles that parallel servers cannot compress. However, this delay limits onboarding throughput and penalizes energy-constrained devices.
